cost.cache_desc: Reuses the parts that are the same every turn (tool definitions, persona, …) to lower input-token cost and latency. Bedrock Claude models only. Default: off.
cost.cache_ttl_desc: 1 hour costs more to write; it suits conversations with long pauses.
cost.cache_unsupported: The current model does not support the prompt cache. Turning it on has no effect.
cost.context_desc: Large tool results are stored in the data directory and only their beginning stays in the conversation; when the conversation grows long, the older part is summarized (this calls the model). Not used with models that keep the history on the server. Default: off.
cost.context_enabled: Offload large tool results and summarize long conversations
cost.ctx_compression_threshold_desc: Summarize when the input reaches this share of the context (above 0, up to 1). Default: 0.85.
cost.ctx_context_window_tokens_desc: Empty = automatic (model settings, the capability table, else 200000). Also used by the chat's context gauge.
cost.ctx_offload_threshold_tokens_desc: Tool results larger than this are offloaded. Default: 1500.
cost.ctx_preview_tokens_desc: How much of an offloaded result stays in the conversation. Smaller than the value above. Default: 750.
cost.ctx_retention_hours_desc: Older offloaded results are deleted (above 0, up to 8760). Default: 24.
cost.ctx_retrieval_max_tokens_desc: The longest read-back of offloaded content at once. Default: 10000.
cost.ctx_summary_ratio_desc: Share of the history summarized at once (0.1–0.8). Default: 0.8.
cost.desc: The length limit of one reply and the features that save tokens. Saved together with the footer's "Save" (to gateway-config.json).
cost.err_env_pinned: Pinned by the environment variable {env}; it cannot be changed here.
cost.err_out_of_range_open: Enter more than {min} and at most {max}.
cost.err_preview_below_offload: Must be smaller than the offload size ({limit}).
cost.output_auto_desc: {n} tokens for the current model (the smaller of its limit and 32,000). Taken again when you switch models.
cost.output_auto_desc_thinking: {n} tokens for the current model: the smaller of its limit and 32,000 for the reply plus {reserve} for thinking. Taken again when you switch models.
cost.output_auto_desc_unknown: {n} tokens for the current model: the provider's default, as this model's limit is not recorded. Taken again when you switch models.
cost.output_fixed_desc: Raise it when replies are cut off. It is a ceiling: you pay only for the tokens actually produced.
cost.output_model_limit: Documented limit of this model: {limit} tokens.
cost.output_model_limit_unknown: This model's limit is not recorded.
cost.output_thinking: Thinking tokens count toward the output limit too.
cost.output_warn_over: Above the model's limit ({limit}). The provider may reject the request.
cost.output_warn_unknown: This model's limit is unknown. A value above it may be rejected by the provider (automatic: {auto}).
cost.output_auto_warn_unknown: Reasoning models can use this up on thinking alone. If you know the model's limit, set a number.
cost.pinned_live: Shown: the value in use now. Once the variable is removed, the saved value is used.
cost.pinned_unknown: Its value is not shown here; while the chat server runs, the page shows the value in use.

diagnostics.finding_apparmor: AppArmor is present; it may deny writes.
diagnostics.finding_classifier_missing: Emotion classification: Sokudan is chosen in the settings but not installed. The rule-based fallback runs.
diagnostics.finding_classifier_rule_chos: Emotion classification: the rule-based classifier is in use (chosen in the settings).
diagnostics.finding_classifier_rule_only: Emotion classification: Sokudan is not installed, so only the rule-based classifier runs. Emotions react rarely.
diagnostics.finding_classifier_sokudan: Emotion classification: Sokudan is in use (installed).
diagnostics.finding_controlled_folder_ac: Defender Controlled Folder Access (if on) blocks writes here.
diagnostics.finding_cwd_root: The process runs in "/": relative paths given to other tools would resolve there (Stira's file tools anchor them at the workspace).
diagnostics.finding_floor: On the identity floor: the write test is skipped by design.
diagnostics.finding_icloud: Managed by iCloud / a file provider: files may be evicted or synced.
diagnostics.finding_missing: Does not exist yet (created on the first write).
diagnostics.finding_onedrive: Under OneDrive: files on demand may be offline.
diagnostics.finding_path_length: Path is close to the 260 limit.
diagnostics.finding_quarantine: Has the quarantine attribute (downloaded content). Files created here may be treated as untrusted.
diagnostics.finding_selinux: SELinux is present; it may deny writes.
diagnostics.finding_page_check_ready: page_check (verification browser: opens a workspace page with no network, runs a few input actions and checks, takes screenshots) is available.
diagnostics.finding_page_check_no_browse: page_check (verification browser) is hidden: no Chrome, Chromium or Edge was found. Install one or set STIRA_BROWSER_PATH.
diagnostics.finding_page_check_platform: page_check (verification browser) is hidden: Windows is not supported yet.
diagnostics.finding_page_check_root: page_check (verification browser) is hidden: Stira runs as root, and the browser would need its sandbox switched off.
diagnostics.finding_run_checks_off: run_checks (verification runner) is off: gateway-config.json run_checks: {"phase": 1} turns it on.
diagnostics.finding_run_checks_ready: run_checks runs the project's checks in a throwaway copy inside a macOS sandbox profile (network, home reads and writes outside refused; self-test passed). Memory is not limited on macOS. A saved Always is effective here.
diagnostics.finding_run_checks_limits_on: run_checks is limits only on this host: the network, home reads and writes outside the copy are NOT held, every call is a card, and a saved Always is read as Ask.
diagnostics.finding_run_checks_self_test: run_checks is limits only: the sandbox self-test failed. The network, home reads and writes outside the copy are NOT held, and a saved Always is read as Ask.
diagnostics.finding_run_checks_platform: run_checks is not registered: Windows is not supported.
diagnostics.finding_run_checks_root: run_checks is not registered: Stira runs as root.
diagnostics.finding_tcc_zone: Inside macOS privacy-protected {zone}: not inspected (that could open a consent dialog).
diagnostics.finding_unresolvable: Cannot resolve the path (for example a symlink loop).
diagnostics.fix_acl: An access control list (ACL) denies the write. Review it yourself (Finder Get Info > Sharing & Permissions, or ls -le), then retry once.
diagnostics.fix_breaker: The circuit breaker blocks writes. Wait until it recovers, or approve the call.
diagnostics.fix_consent_blocked: Stira's approval gate refused the call (no approval for this exact call). Approve it on its approval card, or ask the agent again.
diagnostics.fix_identity_protected: This is an identity or protected file (SOUL, IPD, protected directories). By design no approval or setting lets the agent write it.
diagnostics.fix_install_jev: In your own terminal run pip install -e ".[jev]" to install Sokudan, then restart the server (Stira installs nothing itself).
diagnostics.fix_locked_flag: The file or its folder is locked (uchg). Clear 'Locked' in Finder's Get Info, or run chflags nouchg <path> yourself in a terminal, then retry once.
diagnostics.fix_locked_flag_system: A system-immutable flag (schg etc.) is set. Only an administrator can clear it, outside Stira (sometimes only in recovery mode). Prefer writing somewhere else.
diagnostics.fix_os: The operating system refused the write. Check the location, then retry once.
diagnostics.fix_secret_path: This path is on the secret-path floor (credentials, keys, keychains, browser profiles, .env files). By design no write root, setting or approval lets file tools write it; edit it yourself if you really need to.
diagnostics.fix_os_protection: The command would change an OS protection (file flags, extended attributes, privacy settings, SIP) or use sudo. Stira refuses tool calls that name such commands; do it yourself if you really want to.
diagnostics.fix_other: The cause could not be determined. Read the message, then retry once.
diagnostics.fix_outside_write_roots: The path is outside the agent's write roots. If it should be writable, add the folder to write_roots in Settings (applies after a restart).
diagnostics.fix_permission_denied: The user running Stira lacks write permission (owner/mode). Change it yourself (Finder Get Info > Sharing & Permissions) or use another folder, then retry once.
diagnostics.fix_readonly_attr: The read-only attribute or an immutable flag is set. Clear it yourself as the owner/administrator, then retry once.
diagnostics.fix_readonly_volume: The volume is mounted read-only. Remount it writable or choose a folder on a writable volume, then retry once.
diagnostics.fix_sip: System Integrity Protection guards this location. It cannot be written and SIP should not be disabled; write inside the workspace instead.
diagnostics.fix_tcc: macOS privacy protection (Files and Folders) guards this location. Recommended: keep the working folder outside protected folders (e.g. ~/projects/...) and add it to write_roots. Otherwise allow the app above under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Files and Folders. Full Disk Access is not recommended (far too broad).
diagnostics.fix_wrong_cwd: A relative (or empty) path was resolved against the wrong directory. Use an absolute path or one relative to the agent workspace.
diagnostics.human_only: Stira's diagnosis does not remove OS protections for you; a person carries out the steps above.
diagnostics.no_retry: Retrying does not resolve this failure
diagnostics.principal_launchd: The executable itself, started by launchd ({executable}). A Homebrew build may lose the permission after an update (unverified).
diagnostics.principal_terminal: The terminal app that started Stira ({name})
diagnostics.recheck_clear: The cause is gone; the retry was requested.
diagnostics.recheck_unverified: This cause cannot be checked; the retry was requested.
diagnostics.retry_prompt: I fixed the permission problem. Please retry the {tool} ({operation}) write that just failed, unchanged, once.
diagnostics.skip_changed: the folder changed while it was checked
diagnostics.skip_no_policy: the write policy could not be built from the settings
diagnostics.tab_config_error: Configuration error: the write policy cannot be built from the settings. Fix write_roots and related settings (stira doctor exits with status 2).
diagnostics.tab_desc: The result of the pre-flight check of the write locations (the same check as stira doctor). This section is read-only and changes no setting; fixing a problem is a person's job.

procreview.effective_next_start: An approved rule enters the system prompt's "Procedural Rules" after the server restarts (the newest {n} rules).

procreview.request_failed: The request could not be sent. Its outcome is unknown: check the list after it reloads.
procreview.breaker_notice: The breaker is at {level}: proposals cannot be approved until it is back at NORMAL. Rejecting still works.
procreview.breaker_unknown: The breaker level cannot be read: proposals cannot be approved now. Rejecting still works.
procreview.refused_breaker: Not approved: approving needs the breaker at NORMAL ({code}). Nothing was written; try again once it is back at NORMAL. Rejecting still works.
procreview.refused_breaker_unavailable: Not approved: the breaker level cannot be read ({code}). Nothing was written.
procreview.diff: Diff against the existing rule of the same name
procreview.problem_E_TARGET_EXISTS: A rule of this name exists and this proposal was not made as its revision. It cannot be approved (reject it).
procreview.problem_E_REVISION_STALE: The existing rule changed after this proposal. It cannot be approved (reject it and have it proposed again).
procreview.problem_E_SOURCE_TURN_REQUIRE: It has no source turn, so it cannot be approved.

hb.ceil_desc: The gap when things are calm. Default: 180 minutes (3 hours).
hb.desc: Keeps decaying emotions, recording the state and checking the breaker at intervals, also while nobody is talking. It never calls a model, so it costs no tokens.
hb.enabled_desc: When off, decay is still worked out at the next turn. When on, the state between conversations also shows in the graph. Default: off.
hb.err_floor_above_ceil: The shortest interval must not be longer than the longest ({limit}).
hb.err_intervals_reset: the config file's shortest interval was longer than its longest one
hb.err_lock: another process runs the heartbeat for this data directory
hb.err_unsafe_lock: heartbeat.lock is not a safe file
hb.floor_desc: The gap when the state is unstable. Default: 5 minutes.
hb.internals: Saved in gateway-config.json as hb_enabled / hb_interval_floor_sec / hb_interval_ceil_sec (seconds). The chat server reads them when it starts, so a saved change applies after a restart. When the environment variable STIRA_HEARTBEAT (1 / 0) is set, it decides the switch. This page only sets and shows; there is no button that runs or stops a tick.
hb.interval_hint: The more stable, the closer to the longest interval; the less stable, the closer to the shortest. 1 minute to 24 hours (1440 minutes).
hb.live_degraded: Running, but the last {n} ticks failed. Check the server log.
hb.live_ended: It was on, but it stopped ({reason}). A restart starts it again.
hb.live_not_started: On, but it could not start ({reason}).
hb.live_unknown: The status is shown while the chat server runs.
hb.note_ceil_raised: The longest interval follows the shortest: now {to}.
hb.note_floor_lowered: The shortest interval follows the longest: now {to}.
hb.note_intervals_reset: The config file's shortest interval is longer than its longest one (an omitted one counts as its default, 5 minutes or 3 hours), so the heartbeat does not start. Saving other settings does not fix it: enter the intervals and save (for the defaults, enter 5 and 180 minutes). The heartbeat starts after a restart.
hub.advanced_desc: Information you normally do not need to change.
hub.bc_desc: When recent stability swings so much that the coherence score drops below this, the agent enters "Coherence".
hub.board_confirm_check: I understand that SVG in replies is shown as images
hub.board_confirm_title: Show SVG pictures on the board?
hub.board_internals: Saved in gateway-config.json as ui.board_svg (written only when off). Applies when the Stage page is opened again. The chat page and the Stage log keep showing code. Limits: one SVG up to 32 KB, 500 elements and 8 levels of nesting; 4 per reply.
hub.board_stage_off: The Stage is off now (STIRA_STAGE is not set). You can save this, but nothing changes until the Stage is turned on.
hub.board_svg: Show static SVG on the board
hub.board_svg_desc: Draws a reply's ```svg block as an image rebuilt from allowed shapes, colours and text only. Scripts, links, outside images or fonts and animation are not used and nothing is loaded. Parts that are not allowed are left out; a block that cannot be read or is too large stays code. Default: on.
hub.breaker_desc: Stability runs from 0 to 1; lower means less stable. Higher thresholds restrict earlier, which is safer.
hub.breaker_internals: Stored in agent-config.json under stira_config_overrides. Each enter line stays below its leave line (raising an enter line to or past its leave line raises the leave line with it).
hub.clamped_bc_window: The coherence window in the config file was below 5, so 5 is used. Saving writes 5 to the file.
hub.clamped_hitl_timeout: The approval wait in the config file was out of range, so a rounded value is used. Saving fixes the file.
hub.clamped_protected_layers: Layers 3 to 5 were missing from the protected layers in the config file; they are added back.
hub.classifier_desc: Choose how your messages are judged for their effect on the agent's emotions (trust, vigilance, …).
hub.classifier_internals: Stored in gateway-config.json (jev_enabled / jev_classifier). "Automatic" means jev_enabled=false: SokudanClassifier when Sokudan is installed, otherwise RuleBasedClassifier.
hub.cls_auto_desc: Uses Sokudan when it is installed, otherwise the rule-based method.
hub.cls_rule_desc: Rule-driven judgement that needs nothing extra installed.
hub.cls_running_expected: Will run: {name} (loaded on the first message)
hub.cls_running_unknown: This server does not run an agent, so the method in use cannot be shown.
hub.cls_sokudan_desc: Judges Japanese messages in more detail. Needs a separate install.
hub.cls_unresolved: not decided yet (set by the first message)
hub.crit_desc: Below this, the agent enters "Critical": replies and reads continue; write/exec tools are either stopped (read-only) or need a human approval for every call ("Effective" under Tool permissions shows which). Keep it below the warning line.
hub.danger_banner_hint: You can return to a safe combination from "Safety presets".
hub.danger_board_svg: The board shows images built from the agent's replies (static SVG). Only allowed shapes, colours and text are used, with no script and nothing loaded, but the agent decides what they look like (it can draw a misleading picture).
hub.danger_breaker_low: The breaker thresholds are so low that it will hardly ever trip.
hub.danger_sycophancy_off: The sycophancy alert is practically off: it would only fire when (almost) every recent reply agrees, or its window is under 10 replies and never scores.
hub.danger_trust_all: "Allow everything" ignores Never choices and the shell allowlist.
hub.defaults_staged: Defaults (standard) are in the draft; nothing changes until you save.
hub.delegation_enabled: Let the agent hand tasks to a sub-agent (delegate)
hub.delegation_enabled_desc: The agent can hand reading-heavy research, an independent piece of work or a check to a child agent and gets back only its summary (at most 2,000 characters). The child uses only tools the agent may use without asking. Each hand-off shows an approval card (a YOLO window does not approve it automatically). The stop button stops the child too. Default: on.
hub.delegation_internals: Saved in gateway-config.json under delegation (only values that differ from the defaults are written). Applies from the next turn. Children run one at a time and a child cannot start a child. The chat shows only the names of a child's tool calls (no arguments or results). A child's tokens count in the turn's usage.
hub.delegation_limits_desc: A child that reaches a limit stops there and returns its summary so far and the reason. Defaults: 40 calls, 600 seconds, 20 per turn.
hub.agent_jobs_budget: Tokens per day (all agent jobs together)
hub.agent_jobs_budget_desc: Counted per UTC day. A job that would go over does not run and is paused. It cannot be unlimited. Default: 50,000.
hub.agent_jobs_enabled: Run agent jobs a person defined
hub.agent_jobs_enabled_desc: The scheduler runs a prompt a person registered and confirmed, on the model, while nobody is present. Only read-only tools are available; the run stops at the first write, outbound or approval-needing call. Runs only while the heartbeat is healthy, and jobs come up paused after a restart (a person resumes them). Default: off.
hub.agent_jobs_internals: Saved in gateway-config.json under agent_jobs (only values that differ from the defaults are written). Applies from the next start of the chat server. STIRA_SCHEDULER=0 still turns the whole scheduler off. A job's result is stored as untrusted data inside a fixed frame. An interrupted run is never resumed after a restart.
hub.danger_agent_jobs_on: The model runs on a schedule without a person present (read-only tools only, within the daily token pool).
hub.det_bc_window_desc: How many recent stability values the coherence score uses. 5 to 200 (below 5 there is no score; the larger, the later a swing is noticed).
hub.det_cooldown_desc: The fewest turns before Critical can be cleared. 3 to 50.
hub.det_decay_desc: The shortest interval between steps that ease emotions back to baseline. 0 or more.
hub.det_hitl_rounds_desc: How many times a request may be edited and sent again during an approval. 0 to 10.
hub.det_hitl_timeout_desc: How long an approval waits for a person. 1 second to 24 hours (86400). An expired request counts as denied (the safe side).
hub.det_syc_desc: A sycophancy warning is raised when the recent share of agreement goes above this. 0 to 1.
hub.det_syc_window_desc: How many recent replies the agreement share counts. 1 to 200.
hub.display_desc: How this page looks. Stored in this browser only and applied immediately.
hub.err_broad_root: A filesystem or drive root, the home directory or its ancestors cannot be used: {roots}
hub.err_invalid_root: Only @workspace, absolute paths and paths starting with ~/ are allowed: {roots}
hub.err_must_be_below_warning: Must be below the warning line ({limit}).
hub.err_must_be_below_warning_exit: Must be below the warning's leave line ({limit}).
hub.err_not_installed: Not installed, so it cannot be chosen.
hub.fixed_reason_layers: Protection of Layer 3 and above. It cannot be removed (layers can only be added in the config file).
hub.fixed_reason_server: The chat server decides this value; a saved value is not used.
hub.history_desc: Changes saved from this page and the model section, newest first. "Undo this change" saves a new change that restores the values from before it. Secret values are never recorded.
hub.mode_custom: Allow only the tools I pick (recommended)
hub.mode_custom_desc: Only tools set to Always or Ask below are used.
hub.mode_trust_all_desc: Ignores Never below and allows every tool (Ask tools and exec tools still ask), and skips the shell allowlist. Saving asks for confirmation.
hub.model_desc: Choose the AI model used for the conversation and who provides it (the provider).
hub.model_internals: Stored in agent-config.json (provider / model_override / base_url / api_key_env). Environment variables such as STIRA_PROVIDER and STIRA_MODEL take precedence when set.
hub.note_exit_clamped: The leave line can only sit above the enter line ({enter}), so it is {exit}.
hub.note_exit_raised: The leave line moved up to {exit} too (it must stay above the enter line).
hub.note_saved_above_limit: The saved value {value} is above the limit of {max}. Other settings still save as it is; to change it, use {max} or less.
hub.note_rounded: “{from}” is outside the allowed range, so it is {to}.
hub.note_breaker_pairs_reset: The breaker values in the config file do not form valid pairs (an enter line at or above its leave line, or the critical line at or above the warning line; an omitted value counts as its default). The file's values are shown below, but the breaker runs on the defaults (warning 0.5/0.6, critical 0.3/0.45, coherence 0.6/0.7), or on the stricter of those and the values in use if the file was edited while running. Saving other settings leaves the file as it is: enter a valid set and save; it applies from the next turn.
hub.note_warning_exit_raised: The warning's leave line moved up to {exit} to stay above the critical one.
hub.page_desc: Change model, emotion classification, safety and tool settings on this one page. Nothing takes effect until you press Save below.
hub.pair_sum_critical: Critical below {enter}; cleared above {exit} after at least {turns} turns.
hub.pair_sum_warning: Warning below {enter}, cleared above {exit}. In between, the current state is kept.
hub.preset_developer_desc: Allows every tool except execution tools, including sending to other hosts. Default breaker. Execution tools can only be enabled by environment variable.
hub.preset_safe_desc: Allows read tools only and trips the breaker earlier. For first use or public settings.
hub.preset_staged: "{name}" is in the draft. Press Save to confirm.
hub.preset_standard_desc: Allows reading and writes that stay on this machine. Sending to other hosts (HTTP request, webhook, connected APIs) is off. Default breaker.
hub.presets_desc: Switch tool permissions and the breaker together. Choosing one shows what changes; "Put in draft" then Save confirms it. Execution tools stay off in every preset.
hub.rollback_conflict: Settings were changed elsewhere. The latest values are loaded; try again.
hub.rollback_needs_clean: Save or discard your unsaved changes first.
hub.safety_desc: Decide when write/exec tools are restricted because the agent is becoming unstable (the breaker) and which tools it may use. The breaker does not stop replies.
hub.save_conflict: Settings were changed elsewhere. The latest values are loaded and your changes are kept; review them and save again.
hub.save_failed_model: Switching the model failed, so nothing else was saved.
hub.show_internal_desc: Show internal identifiers such as tool names next to the descriptions (for developers).
hub.status_reason_breaker_pairs_reset: the file's values are not valid pairs; running on the defaults or stricter
hub.tool_batch_desc: Calls several tools at once; it can reach the shell.
hub.tool_cron_desc: Registers jobs that run on a schedule.
hub.tool_current_time_desc: Reads the current date and time.
hub.tool_editor_desc: Edits parts of files (protected files excluded).
hub.tool_file_read_desc: Reads local files within the allowed paths.
hub.tool_file_write_desc: Creates or overwrites files (protected files excluded).
hub.tool_handoff_to_user_desc: Hands the conversation back to you when a decision is needed.
hub.tool_http_request_desc: Sends requests to any URL (leaves this machine).
hub.tool_image_reader_desc: Reads image files; "View images" is the bounded alternative.
hub.tool_journal_desc: Writes notes to a journal file.
hub.tool_lsp_diagnostics_desc: Checks code for errors with a language server.
hub.tool_lsp_hover_desc: Looks up types and docs with a language server.
hub.tool_memory_desc: Stores to and searches a Bedrock Knowledge Base.
hub.tool_oauth_api_call_desc: Calls the API of a service connected via OAuth (leaves this machine).
hub.tool_perplexity_search_desc: Searches the web through the Perplexity API (needs an API key).
hub.tool_stop_desc: Lets the agent end the current run.
hub.tool_think_desc: Runs extra inner reasoning loops; it reuses tools, so it is an execution tool.
hub.tool_use_agent_desc: Starts another agent to do a task.
hub.tool_web_fetch_desc: Fetches the page at a URL.
hub.tool_web_search_desc: Searches the web (needs STIRA_WEB_SEARCH_ENDPOINT; without it the model is not offered this tool).
hub.tool_webhook_send_desc: Sends notifications to registered endpoints (leaves this machine).
hub.tools_desc: Choose the tools the agent may use. While the breaker is at Warning or above, write/exec tools stop or need a human approval for every call, even if allowed here.
hub.tools_internals: Stored in tool-config.json (mode = custom / trust_all, enabled_tools, shell_allowlist). Execution tools (shell, batch, cron, use_agent, swarm, graph, think) are not exposed unless STIRA_ENABLE_EXEC_TOOLS is set.
hub.warn_desc: Below this, the agent enters "Warning" and write/exec tools are stopped (reads continue).
hub.write_custom_desc: List absolute paths below, one per line. @workspace stands for the workspace.
hub.write_desc: Places the file tools (file_write / editor) may write to. Writes anywhere else are denied. Protected files such as SOUL and procedural memory stay read-only whatever is chosen here.
hub.write_internals: Stored in agent-config.json as write_roots (default ["@workspace"]). @workspace is workspace_dir, or the chat server's data directory when unset. Writes outside are denied (write_outside_action = deny). Applies when the chat server restarts.
hub.write_workspace_desc: Only inside the agent's working directory (default: .local/stira/).
hub.write_workspace_unknown: @workspace is the chat server's data directory (shown while the server runs).
hub.read_desc: Places the file-reading tools (file_read / view_image / image_reader / editor view / lsp_*) may read. Anything else is refused (E_READ_OUTSIDE_ROOTS). Keys, credentials, keychains and browser profiles (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, *.pem …) are never readable, whatever is chosen here (E_READ_SECRET_PATH).
hub.read_workspace_desc: Only inside the agent's working directory.
hub.read_workspace_home_desc: Also everything under the home directory (secret paths excepted).
hub.read_everywhere_desc: Any file on this machine (secret paths excepted). Keep it only as long as needed.
hub.read_custom_desc: List absolute paths below, one per line (a repository to read, for example). @workspace stands for the workspace.
hub.read_internals: Stored in agent-config.json as read_roots (default ["@workspace"]). A save that adds a place is confirmed and recorded in the history. read_secret_paths in agent-config.json adds entries to the secret-path floor (they cannot be removed). Applies when the chat server restarts.
hub.danger_read_roots_widened: The file-reading tools may read more places. What the agent reads goes into the conversation (key and credential files stay unreadable whatever is chosen).
hub.danger_write_roots_widened: The file-writing tools may write more places (key and credential files, .env and the like stay unwritable whatever is chosen).
hub.err_empty_roots: At least one place is required.

observer.anchors_saved_note: Saved in agent-config.json (or the built-in defaults). The chat server reads them at start-up: a change applies after a restart.

policy.approvals_link: Approval requests from "Ask" tools appear in the chat and on the Approvals page
policy.danger_loosened: This loosens tool settings (Never → Ask/Always, Ask → Always, a command added to the shell allowlist, or "Allow everything").
policy.danger_recover: This recovers the locked tool rules with these choices (clears the rollback/tampering lock).
policy.err_audit_failed: The change could not be recorded in the history, so nothing was loosened.
policy.err_breaker_active: Tool rules cannot be loosened while the breaker is active (tightening still works).
policy.err_locked: The tool rules are locked. Save with the recovery confirmation (type RECOVER).
policy.err_needs_tool_names: Type the names of the write/external tools being made Always.
policy.err_secret_command: A command containing a secret (a token or password) cannot be added to the allowlist.
policy.err_secret_command_saved: The allowlist holds {count} saved command(s) that look like they contain a secret (a token or password). Remove them to save the tool settings.
policy.floor_data_dir: The data directory is protected from file tools
policy.floor_data_dir_desc: Stores, logs, head anchors, locks, checkpoints and the semantic memory layer cannot be written by file_write / editor, approved or not. Writable: {dirs}.
policy.floor_data_dir_none: Stores, logs, head anchors, locks, checkpoints and the semantic memory layer cannot be written by file_write / editor, approved or not. Nothing in the data directory is a write root now.
policy.floor_data_dir_read_desc: Readable by file_read / view_image / image_reader / editor view / lsp_*: {dirs} only. The tool rules, approvals, checkpoints, Neural State and the other stores cannot be read, approved or not. Outside the data directory: only inside the read roots (#457, see Where files may be read).
policy.floor_data_dir_read_none: Nothing in the data directory is readable by file_read / view_image / image_reader / editor view / lsp_*, approved or not. Outside the data directory: only inside the read roots (#457, see Where files may be read).
policy.floor_desc: These protections are shown read-only. There are no controls here.
policy.floor_exec_off: Hidden (exposed only with {env}; even then never Always)
policy.floor_exec_on: Exposed by {env}. None can be Always; every call asks
policy.floor_identity_desc: {files} and {n} configured path(s). No tool and no approval can write them.
policy.floor_os: Commands that lift OS protections are refused
policy.floor_os_desc: Commands naming {commands} are never run; a person does that by hand if needed.
policy.floor_title: Protections (floor) — no setting or approval lifts these
policy.grant_common: Persistent grant for tools set to Always (same for every tool) — Scope: any arguments of that tool / Expires: when revoked (no automatic expiry) / Revoke: change that tool to Ask or Never in this list and save. The breaker and the floor still apply.
policy.grant_short: Yes (scope, expiry and how to revoke: see the note at the top of this section)
policy.grant_unbounded: No persistent grant: its scope cannot be bounded
policy.help: Choose Always, Ask or Never per tool. The effective decision is the strictest of this rule, the breaker and the protections (floor). Loosening needs a confirmation and is refused while the breaker is active.
policy.internals: Ask tools are stored in ask_tools in tool-config.json; a tool missing from enabled_tools is Never. Exec-class tools, page_check (phase 1) and propose_procedure cannot be Always.
policy.isolation_help: "Isolation" says whether a tool runs in an OS sandbox. It is separate from approval: approving a call does not isolate it.
policy.locked_notice: The saved tool rules failed their check ({reason}): they may have been rolled back, deleted or edited by hand, so every tool is Never (putting the files back does not unlock them). Choose the rules here and save, typing RECOVER, to recover.
policy.names_hint: To make a write/external tool Always, type its internal name(s), separated by spaces or commas.
policy.names_prompt: Type the tool names being made Always: {names}
policy.reason_breaker_critical: CRITICAL: the breaker's action is not known here, so every tool is stopped (fail-closed)
policy.reason_breaker_critical_halt: CRITICAL: every write/exec call needs a human approval
policy.reason_breaker_warning: WARNING: writes/exec need confirmation (no confirmation route, so stopped)
policy.reason_not_configured: off in this server's configuration; turn it on in the config file and restart
policy.reason_floor_constraints: writes to protected targets always refused
policy.reason_rule_always_capped: saved Always, read as Ask: this host's sandbox is not verified (run_checks runs unattended only on a verified macOS sandbox)
policy.secret_saved_notice: The saved allowlist holds {count} command(s) that look like they contain a secret (a token or password), shown masked. Until they are removed and saved, the tool settings cannot be saved.
policy.yolo_help: YOLO approves only tools set to Ask. Always never asks in the first place, and Never does not run during YOLO either.
profile.desc: Pick a common combination in one go. Choosing one shows which tools become Always, Ask or Never. "Put in draft" then Save confirms it (a loosening asks for a confirmation when you save). Your current settings are never rewritten on their own.
profile.dev_desc: Reading as Always; file writes, edits, LSP and shell (allowlisted) as Ask. Nothing is sent out.
profile.minimal_desc: Reading only, as Always. No writes, network or exec. Nothing for YOLO to approve.
profile.outside_table: Tools outside the table (MCP and others) keep their current rule. The shell allowlist does not change.
profile.preview_yolo: Tools YOLO could approve: Internal only {internal} / External allowed {external} / Include exec {exec}
profile.preview_yolo_none: This profile has no Ask tool YOLO covers, so YOLO approves nothing.
profile.research_desc: Development plus fetching and searching the web (web_fetch / web_search / perplexity_search) as Ask.

grants.exec_desc: With the executor on, pressing "Run one iteration" runs exactly one goal iteration in its own session (no automatic next step). A grant issued with "Let the heartbeat start iterations" (off by default, offered only when the server allows it) can also be started by the scheduler's periodic check, at most one iteration per check. Every model and tool call is checked against the grant, and the budget is reserved before each call. A tool set to Ask waits for your approval card (an iteration the heartbeat started stops instead of waiting). A completion claim waits for your verification: only you confirm it. Alpha.
grants.desc: Issue, stop and verify a goal grant with a time limit, a budget and a scope (alpha: it may change). Issuing one runs nothing by itself: an iteration runs only with the executor switch (autonomy.stage_c_exec), when a person presses "Run one iteration" — or, for a grant issued with the heartbeat start (off by default), when the scheduler's check starts one. The goal text is not shown here (only the person who issued it can see it, in the confirmation view).
